# What does this PR do ?
Right now, prefix caching is closely intertwined with the rest of the inference context, making it very difficult to make incremental modifications to the inference context code. This PR factors it all prefix caching logic into separate classes and files so that targeted modifications can be made more easily.

- **Small updates (bug fixes, minor improvements)**: a linked issue is **recommended** and will accelerate the PR review process.

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/auto-sync).

Greptile Summary

This PR refactors prefix caching by extracting the logic from `KVBlockAllocator` and `MambaSlotAllocator` into two new focused classes (`PrefixCacheBlockState`, `PrefixCacheRegistry`) and a `PrefixCachedMambaMetadata` subclass of `MambaMetadata`. The `DynamicInferenceContext` now owns a shared `PrefixCacheRegistry` that both allocators delegate to for hash lookups, registration, and eviction. - **`PrefixCacheBlockState`** takes over per-block tensor bookkeeping (hashes, ref counts, LRU timestamps) that lived inside `KVBlockAllocator`, exposing clean mutation primitives. - **`PrefixCacheRegistry`** centralises all `hash→block_id` maps for KV and Mamba, replacing scattered dicts on the allocators, and owns the cascade-eviction callback wiring. - **`PrefixCachedMambaMetadata`** absorbs intermediate-state extraction buffers and per-request CPU bookkeeping that previously lived on `MambaSlotAllocator`, with `MambaSlotAllocator` slimmed down to cache-pool resources and commit orchestration.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The refactor is a clean structural separation; the core allocation, eviction, and hash-registration paths are functionally equivalent to the old code and all changed tests have been updated to match the new API. The compute_and_store_offsets method still hardcodes mamba_chunk_size=128 while _update_intermediate_metadata uses the configurable self.mamba_chunk_size — a non-default chunk size would produce mismatched filtering and invalid chunk indices. MambaSlotAllocator also has implicit coupling to PrefixCachedMambaMetadata with no runtime guard. megatron/core/inference/contexts/attention_context/mamba_metadata.py (compute_and_store_offsets chunk size mismatch), megatron/core/inference/contexts/mamba_slot_allocator.py (implicit PrefixCachedMambaMetadata dependency in reset and _collect_commit_data)

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | megatron/core/inference/contexts/attention_context/mamba_metadata.py | Adds PrefixCachedMambaMetadata subclass; base class stubs out intermediate-state fields as None; hardcoded mamba_chunk_size=128 in compute_and_store_offsets should use self.mamba_chunk_size. | | megatron/core/inference/contexts/prefix_cache_registry.py | New pure-Python registry; clean KV/Mamba separation with cascade eviction; logic is equivalent to what was scattered across allocators. | | megatron/core/inference/contexts/prefix_cache_block_state.py | New class cleanly encapsulates per-block tensor state (hashes, ref counts, LRU timestamps) with well-documented policy-specific release logic. | | megatron/core/inference/contexts/kv_block_allocator.py | Significantly simplified; all prefix-caching state removed to PrefixCacheBlockState; delegates eviction and allocation bookkeeping cleanly. | | megatron/core/inference/contexts/mamba_slot_allocator.py | Now owns only pool resources and commit orchestration; _collect_commit_data accesses private _intermediate_block_ids_cpu/_eos_cache_block_id_cpu on PrefixCachedMambaMetadata directly; reset() calls reset_intermediate_state() which is only defined on the subclass. | | megatron/core/inference/contexts/dynamic_context.py | Creates PrefixCacheRegistry at context level; switches from isinstance-on-allocator checks to isinstance(mamba_metadata, PrefixCachedMambaMetadata); find_mamba_backoff and _find_kv_match_count now correctly delegate to registry. | | megatron/core/inference/engines/dynamic_engine.py | Small adaptations to use pc_state and prefix_cache_registry instead of direct allocator attributes; functionally equivalent. | | megatron/core/ssm/mamba_mixer.py | Reads intermediate buffers from metadata instead of slot_allocator; uses None-check on metadata field instead of slot_allocator existence check. | Reviews (1): Last reviewed commit: ["Delete test file as a test"](https://github.com/nvidia/megatron-lm/commit/37d08df885b07c330c1f4c16d96be1500954f70f) | [Re-trigger Greptile](https://app.greptile.com/api/retrigger?id=35233296)

The hardcoded `mamba_chunk_size = 128` is inconsistent with `self.mamba_chunk_size` inherited from `MambaMetadata`. `_update_intermediate_metadata` (also in this class) correctly uses `self.mamba_chunk_size` for the same chunk-alignment arithmetic. If the two values ever diverge — e.g. a non-default `mamba_chunk_size` is passed at construction — offsets that pass the filter here would produce invalid chunk indices inside `_update_intermediate_metadata` (e.g. `offset // actual_chunk_size - 1 < 0`). ```suggestion # Use the configured chunk size so this filter stays consistent with # the chunk-index arithmetic in _update_intermediate_metadata. mamba_chunk_size = self.mamba_chunk_size ``` Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

**Implicit dependency on `PrefixCachedMambaMetadata` not enforced** `reset()` calls `self.context.mamba_metadata.reset_intermediate_state()` and `_collect_commit_data()` accesses `metadata._intermediate_block_ids_cpu` / `metadata._eos_cache_block_id_cpu` — both of which are defined only on `PrefixCachedMambaMetadata`. `MambaSlotAllocator` is constructed only when `use_prefix_cached=True` (which guarantees `mamba_metadata` is `PrefixCachedMambaMetadata`), so this is always safe at runtime. However, there is nothing in the call sites to make this relationship explicit, so a future refactor that changes the construction logic would produce a silent `AttributeError` rather than a clear type error. An `assert isinstance(self.context.mamba_metadata, PrefixCachedMambaMetadata)` guard in `__init__`, or typing `context.mamba_metadata` as `PrefixCachedMambaMetadata` in `MambaSlotAllocator.__init__`, would make the coupling explicit.

this PR moves snapshot records into `PrefixCachedMambaMetadata`, but `_collect_commit_data` still reads its private arrays. could the metadata class return a ready-to-save list, so changing the record layout doesn’t also require changing the allocator?

an example flow:

- request A has one snapshot and request B has two.
- we change the metadata to store those three records in one list instead of separate rows for each request.
- today, the allocator must also change because it reads those rows directly.
- with a ready-to-save method, that storage-layout change could stay entirely inside the metadata class.

this PR allocates temporary GPU buffers in `PrefixCachedMambaMetadata` before `_allocate_mamba_cache` checks the configured budget. could we check the budget first, so an invalid setting produces a clear budget error instead of potentially running out of GPU memory?

an example flow:

- a user sets a 1 GB cache budget, but the settings require 2 GB of temporary space.
- only 1.5 GB is free, so allocating the temporary buffers fails before the budget check.
- checking first would report that the 1 GB budget is too small, without trying the allocation.
Addressed this; take a new look please

Greptile Summary

This PR refactors prefix caching by extracting the logic from `KVBlockAllocator` and `MambaSlotAllocator` into two new focused classes (`PrefixCacheBlockState`, `PrefixCacheRegistry`) and a `PrefixCachedMambaMetadata` subclass of `MambaMetadata`. The `DynamicInferenceContext` now owns a shared `PrefixCacheRegistry` that both allocators delegate to for hash lookups, registration, and eviction. - **`PrefixCacheBlockState`** takes over per-block tensor bookkeeping (hashes, ref counts, LRU timestamps) that lived inside `KVBlockAllocator`, exposing clean mutation primitives. - **`PrefixCacheRegistry`** centralises all `hash→block_id` maps for KV and Mamba, replacing scattered dicts on the allocators, and owns the cascade-eviction callback wiring. - **`PrefixCachedMambaMetadata`** absorbs intermediate-state extraction buffers and per-request CPU bookkeeping that previously lived on `MambaSlotAllocator`, with `MambaSlotAllocator` slimmed down to cache-pool resources and commit orchestration.

Confidence Score: 4/5

The refactor is a clean structural separation; the core allocation, eviction, and hash-registration paths are functionally equivalent to the old code and all changed tests have been updated to match the new API. The compute_and_store_offsets method still hardcodes mamba_chunk_size=128 while _update_intermediate_metadata uses the configurable self.mamba_chunk_size — a non-default chunk size would produce mismatched filtering and invalid chunk indices. MambaSlotAllocator also has implicit coupling to PrefixCachedMambaMetadata with no runtime guard. megatron/core/inference/contexts/attention_context/mamba_metadata.py (compute_and_store_offsets chunk size mismatch), megatron/core/inference/contexts/mamba_slot_allocator.py (implicit PrefixCachedMambaMetadata dependency in reset and _collect_commit_data)
